transcript:
1
00:00:00,090 --> 00:00:02,760
- This is the largest
amount of spider silk

2
00:00:02,760 --> 00:00:05,070
that's ever been put together
for a test like this.

3
00:00:05,070 --> 00:00:06,720
So I'm gonna put it to the ultimate test,

4
00:00:06,720 --> 00:00:09,330
and try to be the first
person ever to swing

5
00:00:09,330 --> 00:00:10,290
from spider silk.

6
00:00:10,290 --> 00:00:12,420
I don't know if it's going to
hold my weight, so let's see.

7
00:00:12,420 --> 00:00:16,733
In three, two, one.
(Derek yelling)

8
00:00:17,760 --> 00:00:18,630
- In "Spider-Man Two,"

9
00:00:18,630 --> 00:00:21,180
Peter Parker is on a runaway
train full of passengers.

10
00:00:21,180 --> 00:00:22,530
And to stop it from derailing,

11
00:00:22,530 --> 00:00:24,060
he stands in front of the train,

12
00:00:24,060 --> 00:00:27,270
fires webs at the buildings
around him, and holds on.

13
00:00:27,270 --> 00:00:29,490
The webs stretch, some of them snap,

14
00:00:29,490 --> 00:00:31,920
but they do just enough
to slow down the train

15
00:00:31,920 --> 00:00:33,630
and save everyone on board.

16
00:00:33,630 --> 00:00:36,090
It sounds like something
straight out of a comic book.

17
00:00:36,090 --> 00:00:37,500
But real spider silk,

18
00:00:37,500 --> 00:00:39,780
the fiber that makes up a spider's web,

19
00:00:39,780 --> 00:00:42,330
well, it truly might be this incredible.

20
00:00:42,330 --> 00:00:45,060
It's reportedly stronger than
steel. It's pretty strong.

21
00:00:45,060 --> 00:00:46,560
That's crazy!

22
00:00:46,560 --> 00:00:49,440
And 10 times tougher than Kevlar.

23
00:00:49,440 --> 00:00:50,790
To find out if that's really true,

24
00:00:50,790 --> 00:00:52,380
I went to the Blackledge Spider Lab

25
00:00:52,380 --> 00:00:53,640
at the University of Akron,

26
00:00:53,640 --> 00:00:55,440
one of the world's
leading research centers

27
00:00:55,440 --> 00:00:56,877
studying spider silk.

28
00:00:56,877 --> 00:00:58,260
Before I went to the lab,

29
00:00:58,260 --> 00:01:00,180
I'd always assume that
a spiderweb was made

30
00:01:00,180 --> 00:01:01,770
from just one kind of silk.

31
00:01:01,770 --> 00:01:03,660
But that's actually not the case.

32
00:01:03,660 --> 00:01:05,880
One type of silk anchors
the web to a surface.

33
00:01:05,880 --> 00:01:07,860
Another forms this stretchy spiral,

34
00:01:07,860 --> 00:01:10,410
and a different sticky silk catches prey.

35
00:01:10,410 --> 00:01:11,340
Once something's trapped,

36
00:01:11,340 --> 00:01:14,100
the spider switches to yet
another silk to wrap it up.

37
00:01:14,100 --> 00:01:16,560
- The threads are all
thinner than your hair,

38
00:01:16,560 --> 00:01:18,467
so they're going to look
pretty similar to each other

39
00:01:18,467 --> 00:01:20,280
unless you use a microscope.

40
00:01:20,280 --> 00:01:21,113
- [Henry] All in all,

41
00:01:21,113 --> 00:01:22,650
there are seven different types of silk,

42
00:01:22,650 --> 00:01:24,840
but the strongest is the dragline silk,

43
00:01:24,840 --> 00:01:27,120
which holds the web in its place.

44
00:01:27,120 --> 00:01:30,780
- We've got the two main
structural threads in this web.

45
00:01:30,780 --> 00:01:33,330
So the spokes on the wagon wheel

46
00:01:33,330 --> 00:01:36,270
and the outer framework here,
that's all the dragline silk.

47
00:01:36,270 --> 00:01:39,180
It's called major ampullate
silk if you want the fancy word.

48
00:01:39,180 --> 00:01:40,650
- The major ampullate is that one

49
00:01:40,650 --> 00:01:44,010
that commonly compared to steel?

50
00:01:44,010 --> 00:01:45,180
- Yes!
- Okay.

51
00:01:45,180 --> 00:01:46,110
- Absolutely.

52
00:01:46,110 --> 00:01:49,200
And that's partly because it's
function in a web like this.

53
00:01:49,200 --> 00:01:52,920
A bug hits it, to stop that moving bug,

54
00:01:52,920 --> 00:01:55,643
most of the work is done
by the dragline silk.

55
00:01:55,643 --> 00:01:56,476
- [Henry] To do this,

56
00:01:56,476 --> 00:01:58,860
the dragline silk has
to be incredibly strong.

57
00:01:58,860 --> 00:02:00,720
So to find out how it compares to steel,

58
00:02:00,720 --> 00:02:02,220
we wanted to run a test,

59
00:02:02,220 --> 00:02:04,970
but it turns out that getting
the sample isn't so easy.

60
00:02:05,970 --> 00:02:07,860
All right, we've taken
a garden variety spider

61
00:02:07,860 --> 00:02:10,080
and knocked it unconscious using CO2.

62
00:02:10,080 --> 00:02:12,810
We brought it over here and
we put it down with tape.

63
00:02:12,810 --> 00:02:15,840
I then started pulling out
the dragline silk by hand.

64
00:02:15,840 --> 00:02:17,706
It's so light that you can barely feel it.

65
00:02:17,706 --> 00:02:20,250
We've attached it to this
big rotating mechanism

66
00:02:20,250 --> 00:02:22,404
which they custom made to milk spiders.

67
00:02:22,404 --> 00:02:24,987
(bright music)

68
00:02:26,820 --> 00:02:29,730
No spiders were harmed in
the making of this video.

69
00:02:29,730 --> 00:02:30,690
Now that we've got our silk,

70
00:02:30,690 --> 00:02:32,430
we can put one strand into a machine

71
00:02:32,430 --> 00:02:34,470
that slowly pulls on our sample.

72
00:02:34,470 --> 00:02:37,530
And as it pulls, we'll
monitor two key properties.

73
00:02:37,530 --> 00:02:38,610
When you pull on the silk,

74
00:02:38,610 --> 00:02:41,550
that force is spread over a
tiny cross-sectional area.

75
00:02:41,550 --> 00:02:44,790
If you divide the force by
that area, you get the stress.

76
00:02:44,790 --> 00:02:47,340
Now, as you pull, the
silk is also stretching.

77
00:02:47,340 --> 00:02:49,680
To see just how much, we
divide the change in length

78
00:02:49,680 --> 00:02:53,010
by the original length to get
a measure called the strain.

79
00:02:53,010 --> 00:02:54,690
At first, as the stress increases,

80
00:02:54,690 --> 00:02:57,180
the strain increases
roughly in proportion.

81
00:02:57,180 --> 00:02:58,500
And if we stop pulling here,

82
00:02:58,500 --> 00:03:01,170
the silk would spring back
to its original length.

83
00:03:01,170 --> 00:03:03,540
But keep pulling and
eventually it passes a point

84
00:03:03,540 --> 00:03:05,843
where some of that
stretching becomes permanent.

85
00:03:06,690 --> 00:03:08,103
And it's pulling.

86
00:03:08,940 --> 00:03:09,773
- [Videographer] All right.

87
00:03:09,773 --> 00:03:11,160
You film that, I'm going
to be filming this.

88
00:03:11,160 --> 00:03:13,920
- [Henry] And it broke.
- [Videographer] Wow!

89
00:03:13,920 --> 00:03:15,750
- [Henry] Eventually, if you
keep pulling on the silk,

90
00:03:15,750 --> 00:03:16,830
it will break.

91
00:03:16,830 --> 00:03:18,540
And at that point, the force applied,

92
00:03:18,540 --> 00:03:20,130
divided by the cross-sectional area

93
00:03:20,130 --> 00:03:22,380
is called its ultimate tensile strength.

94
00:03:22,380 --> 00:03:25,650
- We're at about 600 megapascals.

95
00:03:25,650 --> 00:03:26,700
- [Henry] To put that in perspective,

96
00:03:26,700 --> 00:03:28,050
if you had a rope of spider silk

97
00:03:28,050 --> 00:03:30,750
that had a cross-sectional
area of one square centimeter,

98
00:03:30,750 --> 00:03:32,550
roughly the size of your little finger,

99
00:03:32,550 --> 00:03:35,970
it could support about
60,000 newtons of force.

100
00:03:35,970 --> 00:03:38,730
That's the weight of a fully
grown African elephant.

101
00:03:38,730 --> 00:03:40,980
And that's not even the
strongest spider silk out there.

102
00:03:40,980 --> 00:03:45,150
- Breaking stress wasn't
incredible for this piece of silk.

103
00:03:45,150 --> 00:03:46,710
- [Henry] Deep in the
jungles of Madagascar

104
00:03:46,710 --> 00:03:48,390
lives the Darwin's bark spider.

105
00:03:48,390 --> 00:03:50,250
Its diet consists of flying insects

106
00:03:50,250 --> 00:03:51,810
that zip over wide rivers.

107
00:03:51,810 --> 00:03:54,150
So to catch its prey,
the Darwin's bark spider

108
00:03:54,150 --> 00:03:57,450
has to spin giant webs that
stretch up to 25 meters

109
00:03:57,450 --> 00:03:59,070
over open water.

110
00:03:59,070 --> 00:04:01,110
And to survive that kind
of distance and tension,

111
00:04:01,110 --> 00:04:03,060
its silk has to be incredibly strong.

112
00:04:03,060 --> 00:04:04,590
It has an ultimate tensile strength

113
00:04:04,590 --> 00:04:07,020
of around 1,600 megapascals.

114
00:04:07,020 --> 00:04:09,300
That's more than twice the
strength of our sample.

115
00:04:09,300 --> 00:04:11,730
But experimental ultra
high strength steels

116
00:04:11,730 --> 00:04:13,290
can reach an ultimate tensile strength

117
00:04:13,290 --> 00:04:15,720
of nearly 3,000 megapascals.

118
00:04:15,720 --> 00:04:18,360
That's about three times that
of typical dragline silk,

119
00:04:18,360 --> 00:04:21,120
but steel is also about six times denser.

120
00:04:21,120 --> 00:04:23,820
So for two ropes with
the same mass and length,

121
00:04:23,820 --> 00:04:26,430
the silk rope has six times
the cross-sectional area.

122
00:04:26,430 --> 00:04:28,710
Six times the area at
one third the strength,

123
00:04:28,710 --> 00:04:30,870
well, that gives a rope that
can take twice the force

124
00:04:30,870 --> 00:04:31,980
before it snaps.

125
00:04:31,980 --> 00:04:33,780
This measure of strength relative to mass

126
00:04:33,780 --> 00:04:35,370
is called specific strength.

127
00:04:35,370 --> 00:04:37,470
And it means that for
the same mass and length,

128
00:04:37,470 --> 00:04:39,900
spiderwebs can withstand
roughly twice the force

129
00:04:39,900 --> 00:04:42,270
of ultra high strength
steel before breaking.

130
00:04:42,270 --> 00:04:44,790
- So that's where ounce for ounce,

131
00:04:44,790 --> 00:04:46,980
spider silk is quite strong.

132
00:04:46,980 --> 00:04:49,080
You got to think about
what is the application

133
00:04:49,080 --> 00:04:51,030
you're talking about
using this material in.

134
00:04:51,030 --> 00:04:53,070
Is it somewhere where you
don't care about weight,

135
00:04:53,070 --> 00:04:54,030
and you need the strength?

136
00:04:54,030 --> 00:04:55,950
Then steel's going to be perfectly fine.

137
00:04:55,950 --> 00:04:57,240
But if weight matters,

138
00:04:57,240 --> 00:04:59,400
spider silk is really the champion there

139
00:04:59,400 --> 00:05:01,560
for tensile strength.

140
00:05:01,560 --> 00:05:03,390
- [Henry] But strength alone isn't enough.

141
00:05:03,390 --> 00:05:05,580
To see why, look at rock climbers.

142
00:05:05,580 --> 00:05:08,070
If a rock climber was just
hanging, all we would care about

143
00:05:08,070 --> 00:05:09,900
was if the rope could
support their weight.

144
00:05:09,900 --> 00:05:14,160
That's strength. But climbers
don't just hang, they fall.

145
00:05:14,160 --> 00:05:16,230
And now the rope has to
bring them to a stop,

146
00:05:16,230 --> 00:05:18,450
which means absorbing that kinetic energy.

147
00:05:18,450 --> 00:05:19,980
Stop the fall in a short distance,

148
00:05:19,980 --> 00:05:22,050
and the energy has to be absorbed quickly.

149
00:05:22,050 --> 00:05:23,910
The forces are enormous.

150
00:05:23,910 --> 00:05:26,760
Stretch it out and that same
energy is absorbed gradually,

151
00:05:26,760 --> 00:05:28,200
so the forces are lower.

152
00:05:28,200 --> 00:05:30,510
So to absorb more energy without snapping,

153
00:05:30,510 --> 00:05:32,310
it has to stretch further.

154
00:05:32,310 --> 00:05:34,800
And that's actually not so
different from spider silk.

155
00:05:34,800 --> 00:05:39,030
- So a bug hits this web,
you've got to stop the flight

156
00:05:39,030 --> 00:05:40,560
of that bug pretty quickly.

157
00:05:40,560 --> 00:05:42,120
And you could do it by just building

158
00:05:42,120 --> 00:05:43,890
a really stiff structure.

159
00:05:43,890 --> 00:05:46,560
Think like a brick wall, you
throw a tennis ball against it.

160
00:05:46,560 --> 00:05:48,750
You're gonna stop that ball instantly.

161
00:05:48,750 --> 00:05:51,427
But that doesn't work very well
if you want to catch a meal.

162
00:05:51,427 --> 00:05:53,070
- It'll bounce off.
- Because it'll just fall out.

163
00:05:53,070 --> 00:05:56,640
And so it helps to slowly
decelerate the insect

164
00:05:56,640 --> 00:05:59,160
so that the web has time to stick to it,

165
00:05:59,160 --> 00:06:02,430
and keep the meal for
the spider to subdue.

166
00:06:02,430 --> 00:06:04,920
- [Henry] So the spider silk
has to be quite stretchy.

167
00:06:04,920 --> 00:06:09,510
- This piece of silk
stretched to 70% of its length

168
00:06:09,510 --> 00:06:10,380
before it broke,

169
00:06:10,380 --> 00:06:12,960
which is really exceptional
for dragline silk.

170
00:06:12,960 --> 00:06:14,550
- [Henry] Now, every
tiny bit of stretching

171
00:06:14,550 --> 00:06:16,110
absorbs a little bit of energy.

172
00:06:16,110 --> 00:06:18,000
If you add all these
tiny amounts together,

173
00:06:18,000 --> 00:06:20,580
the result is the total
energy the material absorbs

174
00:06:20,580 --> 00:06:21,540
before breaking.

175
00:06:21,540 --> 00:06:22,770
On a stress/strain graph,

176
00:06:22,770 --> 00:06:25,140
it's proportional to the
area under the curve.

177
00:06:25,140 --> 00:06:27,360
This is the material's toughness.

178
00:06:27,360 --> 00:06:29,730
Kevlar, the material used
in bulletproof vests,

179
00:06:29,730 --> 00:06:31,860
whose whole job is to take
the energy of a bullet

180
00:06:31,860 --> 00:06:34,290
and spread it out before
it reaches the body, well,

181
00:06:34,290 --> 00:06:37,560
it has a toughness of up to
50 megajoules per cubic meter.

182
00:06:37,560 --> 00:06:39,420
Experimental ultra-high strength steel

183
00:06:39,420 --> 00:06:42,960
has a toughness of around 170
megajoules per cubic meter.

184
00:06:42,960 --> 00:06:44,760
But spider silk?

185
00:06:44,760 --> 00:06:47,280
- This piece of silk had a toughness

186
00:06:47,280 --> 00:06:50,970
of about 205 megajoules per cubic meter.

187
00:06:50,970 --> 00:06:53,580
- Oh, okay. So that might
be like four times Kevlar.

188
00:06:53,580 --> 00:06:55,530
But the silk from the Darwin's bark spider

189
00:06:55,530 --> 00:06:59,310
can have a peak toughness of
520 megajoules per cubic meter.

190
00:06:59,310 --> 00:07:01,680
That's roughly three times
the strongest steel out there,

191
00:07:01,680 --> 00:07:03,630
and 10 times as tough as Kevlar.

192
00:07:03,630 --> 00:07:05,940
See, Kevlar has a very
high tensile strength,

193
00:07:05,940 --> 00:07:07,620
but it's also quite stiff.

194
00:07:07,620 --> 00:07:09,450
Compared with stretchy spider silk,

195
00:07:09,450 --> 00:07:11,910
that means that the
stress/strain graph rises sharply

196
00:07:11,910 --> 00:07:14,430
and fails before it can stretch very far.

197
00:07:14,430 --> 00:07:16,740
So it's not able to absorb as much energy.

198
00:07:16,740 --> 00:07:19,140
And that's why spider
silk wins on toughness.

199
00:07:19,140 --> 00:07:21,300
- But it's the ultimate
in green chemistry.

200
00:07:21,300 --> 00:07:23,430
They're not using the high temperature,

201
00:07:23,430 --> 00:07:27,510
or the caustic solvents that
most of the polymer industry

202
00:07:27,510 --> 00:07:30,060
uses to make high performance threads.

203
00:07:30,060 --> 00:07:33,540
They're doing it at room
temperature, inside a living body,

204
00:07:33,540 --> 00:07:35,130
with the same basic building blocks

205
00:07:35,130 --> 00:07:37,890
that you use to build
your hair and your skin.

206
00:07:37,890 --> 00:07:39,300
- Now, the secret to spider silk's

207
00:07:39,300 --> 00:07:40,890
unbelievable natural strength

208
00:07:40,890 --> 00:07:43,620
lies in how those building
blocks are arranged.

209
00:07:43,620 --> 00:07:45,090
If you look inside a silk fiber,

210
00:07:45,090 --> 00:07:48,240
you'll find spider silk
proteins called spidroins.

211
00:07:48,240 --> 00:07:49,080
In some regions,

212
00:07:49,080 --> 00:07:52,170
the spidroins are arranged
in similar size and shape,

213
00:07:52,170 --> 00:07:54,150
and they're closely
aligned along its length.

214
00:07:54,150 --> 00:07:56,190
They're kind of like stacked egg trays.

215
00:07:56,190 --> 00:07:58,020
These are nanocrystals.

216
00:07:58,020 --> 00:08:00,510
In other areas, the
spidroins aren't so uniform.

217
00:08:00,510 --> 00:08:01,620
Here they're less ordered,

218
00:08:01,620 --> 00:08:04,110
and they can move and
change shape more freely.

219
00:08:04,110 --> 00:08:06,240
These are called the amorphous regions.

220
00:08:06,240 --> 00:08:09,180
Together, they work like a
network of tiny rigid blocks

221
00:08:09,180 --> 00:08:12,090
connected by elastic cords,
which I have in front of me.

222
00:08:12,090 --> 00:08:13,170
When I pull on the network,

223
00:08:13,170 --> 00:08:15,540
the cords stretch, and they absorb energy.

224
00:08:15,540 --> 00:08:16,860
The blocks don't stretch much,

225
00:08:16,860 --> 00:08:18,990
but each one connects to several cords,

226
00:08:18,990 --> 00:08:21,330
which spreads the pull across the network.

227
00:08:21,330 --> 00:08:23,730
So the amorphous regions
let the silk stretch

228
00:08:23,730 --> 00:08:26,910
while the nanocrystals help it
withstand a much larger pull.

229
00:08:26,910 --> 00:08:28,530
Together, they allow the silk to absorb

230
00:08:28,530 --> 00:08:30,600
a tremendous amount of
energy before breaking,

231
00:08:30,600 --> 00:08:32,010
which makes it so tough.

232
00:08:32,010 --> 00:08:34,230
The result is a material
that's stronger than steel

233
00:08:34,230 --> 00:08:37,020
by weight and also tougher than Kevlar.

234
00:08:37,020 --> 00:08:39,180
It sounds perfect for
making climbing ropes,

235
00:08:39,180 --> 00:08:42,450
parachute cords, airbags,
even bulletproof vests.

236
00:08:42,450 --> 00:08:45,030
But we actually aren't using
spider silk for any of that,

237
00:08:45,030 --> 00:08:47,640
even though we've been
trying to for centuries.

238
00:08:47,640 --> 00:08:50,700
In 1709, a Frenchman
named Francois Xavier Bon

239
00:08:50,700 --> 00:08:53,880
painstakingly collected
hundreds of spider egg sacs,

240
00:08:53,880 --> 00:08:57,210
boiled them, combed them like
wool, spun them into thread,

241
00:08:57,210 --> 00:08:58,770
and then used them to make stockings

242
00:08:58,770 --> 00:09:01,470
that attracted the attention
at the royal court.

243
00:09:01,470 --> 00:09:03,300
But this was harder than it sounds.

244
00:09:03,300 --> 00:09:04,133
As he later said,

245
00:09:04,133 --> 00:09:06,450
"The only difficulty now lies in procuring

246
00:09:06,450 --> 00:09:08,130
a sufficient quantity of spider bags

247
00:09:08,130 --> 00:09:10,380
to make any considerable work of it."

248
00:09:10,380 --> 00:09:13,440
Three centuries later, Simon
Peers and Nicholas Godley

249
00:09:13,440 --> 00:09:15,660
led a years long project in Madagascar,

250
00:09:15,660 --> 00:09:17,880
in which teams of
Malagasy workers gathered

251
00:09:17,880 --> 00:09:20,190
more than a million
golden orb weaver spiders

252
00:09:20,190 --> 00:09:21,780
in the jungle by hand.

253
00:09:21,780 --> 00:09:24,360
They extracted their silk
and painstakingly wove

254
00:09:24,360 --> 00:09:27,270
and embroidered it into
a single golden cape.

255
00:09:27,270 --> 00:09:29,910
Why hadn't they tried
farming the spiders instead?

256
00:09:29,910 --> 00:09:32,580
Well, attempts to do that all
run into the same problem.

257
00:09:32,580 --> 00:09:34,920
Spiders are cannibals.

258
00:09:34,920 --> 00:09:38,130
The big problem with spiders
is that they eat each other?

259
00:09:38,130 --> 00:09:39,480
- That's one of the big problems.

260
00:09:39,480 --> 00:09:40,830
And then you can't just keep them

261
00:09:40,830 --> 00:09:42,180
in a tiny little container.

262
00:09:42,180 --> 00:09:43,590
You're going to have to
have a lot of real estate

263
00:09:43,590 --> 00:09:46,950
if you're going to have a farm
with 10,000 spiders on it.

264
00:09:46,950 --> 00:09:48,120
- [Henry] Even if you could get your hands

265
00:09:48,120 --> 00:09:49,890
on that many spiders, as we've seen,

266
00:09:49,890 --> 00:09:51,150
milking them is difficult,

267
00:09:51,150 --> 00:09:53,220
and the spiders don't always cooperate.

268
00:09:53,220 --> 00:09:57,680
- Really cooperative spider
will give you 300 yards of silk.

269
00:09:57,680 --> 00:10:00,000
100's a lot more typical,

270
00:10:00,000 --> 00:10:02,070
but they kind of have their
own individual personalities.

271
00:10:02,070 --> 00:10:04,350
Some of them will just
break the thread right away,

272
00:10:04,350 --> 00:10:06,180
and not even cooperate with you.

273
00:10:06,180 --> 00:10:08,340
- That's why natural
spider silk is so scarce.

274
00:10:08,340 --> 00:10:11,610
One supplier charges
$700 for 100 milligrams,

275
00:10:11,610 --> 00:10:14,940
which works out to roughly
$7 million per kilogram.

276
00:10:14,940 --> 00:10:17,400
That's roughly 50 times the price of gold.

277
00:10:17,400 --> 00:10:19,617
Okay, so we can't farm
spiders for their silk,

278
00:10:19,617 --> 00:10:21,330
but we know what the proteins are,

279
00:10:21,330 --> 00:10:23,130
so surely we can just make them?

280
00:10:23,130 --> 00:10:24,720
Well, scientists have tried.

281
00:10:24,720 --> 00:10:27,750
By the late 1990s, researchers
at DuPont took the genes

282
00:10:27,750 --> 00:10:29,340
that code for spider silk proteins

283
00:10:29,340 --> 00:10:31,830
and put them into E. coli and yeast.

284
00:10:31,830 --> 00:10:34,290
These living cells are
like protein factories.

285
00:10:34,290 --> 00:10:37,140
One engineered cell
quickly becomes millions.

286
00:10:37,140 --> 00:10:37,973
It worked,

287
00:10:37,973 --> 00:10:40,770
but scientists wanted an
even more efficient method.

288
00:10:40,770 --> 00:10:41,970
So in 2001,

289
00:10:41,970 --> 00:10:44,610
a team in Germany tried
implanting spider silk genes

290
00:10:44,610 --> 00:10:46,920
into plants like tobacco and potatoes.

291
00:10:46,920 --> 00:10:49,110
But if you really want to
produce a lot of protein

292
00:10:49,110 --> 00:10:51,990
in a concentrated form, look at milk.

293
00:10:51,990 --> 00:10:52,823
To feed their young,

294
00:10:52,823 --> 00:10:55,770
mothers produce milk with high
concentrations of proteins.

295
00:10:55,770 --> 00:10:57,030
So around the same time,

296
00:10:57,030 --> 00:10:58,680
a Canadian company called Nexia

297
00:10:58,680 --> 00:11:00,210
tried something much stranger.

298
00:11:00,210 --> 00:11:02,387
They put spider silk genes into goats,

299
00:11:02,387 --> 00:11:05,730
creating genetically
modified spider goats.

300
00:11:05,730 --> 00:11:07,530
No, no, really, they made spider goats.

301
00:11:07,530 --> 00:11:11,520
These goats produce milk
chock-full of spider silk proteins.

302
00:11:11,520 --> 00:11:12,600
In one sense, it worked.

303
00:11:12,600 --> 00:11:13,800
All the experiments were able

304
00:11:13,800 --> 00:11:15,510
to produce spider silk proteins,

305
00:11:15,510 --> 00:11:17,730
but they ran into the same problem.

306
00:11:17,730 --> 00:11:19,140
From E. coli or yeast,

307
00:11:19,140 --> 00:11:21,720
these proteins were purified
as a fine white powder.

308
00:11:21,720 --> 00:11:24,510
From plants, the purified
proteins formed a viscous,

309
00:11:24,510 --> 00:11:26,070
gelatin-like liquid.

310
00:11:26,070 --> 00:11:28,440
And from goats, it was
dissolved in the milk.

311
00:11:28,440 --> 00:11:31,200
None of these even vaguely
resemble spider silk.

312
00:11:31,200 --> 00:11:34,440
- And that's one of the
secrets that any company

313
00:11:34,440 --> 00:11:36,720
that really wants to mimic spider silk

314
00:11:36,720 --> 00:11:39,690
at an industrial scale
needs to kind of figure out

315
00:11:39,690 --> 00:11:44,370
is how to process silk
proteins the way spiders do.

316
00:11:44,370 --> 00:11:46,340
- But that's easier said than done.

317
00:11:46,340 --> 00:11:49,200
In a spider, it all
starts in the silk gland

318
00:11:49,200 --> 00:11:50,910
in a region called tail.

319
00:11:50,910 --> 00:11:53,280
Cells here make proteins called spidroins,

320
00:11:53,280 --> 00:11:56,160
and they secrete them into
the fluid inside the gland.

321
00:11:56,160 --> 00:11:58,380
Every spidroin has three main parts.

322
00:11:58,380 --> 00:11:59,940
One end is called the N-terminal,

323
00:11:59,940 --> 00:12:01,530
and the other the C-terminal.

324
00:12:01,530 --> 00:12:03,660
And between them is a
long repeating sequence

325
00:12:03,660 --> 00:12:05,010
of amino acids.

326
00:12:05,010 --> 00:12:06,930
This is called the repetitive region.

327
00:12:06,930 --> 00:12:09,420
Once inside the tail, the
C-terminal ends pair up,

328
00:12:09,420 --> 00:12:11,820
which links neighboring
spidroins together.

329
00:12:11,820 --> 00:12:14,250
But the N-terminal ends
stay mostly separate.

330
00:12:14,250 --> 00:12:16,620
So the spidroins are still
loose enough to bend,

331
00:12:16,620 --> 00:12:18,390
coil, and move around.

332
00:12:18,390 --> 00:12:20,610
Next, they move into the storage sac,

333
00:12:20,610 --> 00:12:23,310
where they're packed together
at high concentrations.

334
00:12:23,310 --> 00:12:24,990
Normally, proteins this concentrated

335
00:12:24,990 --> 00:12:27,390
would stick to each other,
and clump into a solid,

336
00:12:27,390 --> 00:12:30,300
but this can be modified with
a careful balance of salts

337
00:12:30,300 --> 00:12:31,920
and by changing the pH.

338
00:12:31,920 --> 00:12:33,930
The pH is a measure of the concentration

339
00:12:33,930 --> 00:12:35,880
of hydronium ions in a solution.

340
00:12:35,880 --> 00:12:38,760
And because hydrogen ions
are little positive charges,

341
00:12:38,760 --> 00:12:40,500
you can think of the pH like a dial

342
00:12:40,500 --> 00:12:41,970
that controls the electrical charge

343
00:12:41,970 --> 00:12:43,770
on different parts of the protein.

344
00:12:43,770 --> 00:12:45,600
In the storage sac, the pH is tuned

345
00:12:45,600 --> 00:12:48,480
so that the N-terminal ends
carry a net negative charge.

346
00:12:48,480 --> 00:12:50,280
Every protein carries the same charge.

347
00:12:50,280 --> 00:12:53,010
And since like charges repel,
when you crowd them together,

348
00:12:53,010 --> 00:12:55,320
they shove apart instead
of sticking together.

349
00:12:55,320 --> 00:12:56,880
Now, the spidroins are still crowded

350
00:12:56,880 --> 00:12:59,550
in this aqueous solution, and
at such high concentrations,

351
00:12:59,550 --> 00:13:01,500
they begin to gradually rearrange.

352
00:13:01,500 --> 00:13:03,360
The N-terminals are attracted to water.

353
00:13:03,360 --> 00:13:04,680
These are hydrophilic.

354
00:13:04,680 --> 00:13:06,690
While the repetitive
region is repelled by it,

355
00:13:06,690 --> 00:13:08,340
this is hydrophobic.

356
00:13:08,340 --> 00:13:10,080
So the spidroins rearrange,

357
00:13:10,080 --> 00:13:11,850
and you end up having
these hydrophilic parts

358
00:13:11,850 --> 00:13:13,590
facing outward towards the water.

359
00:13:13,590 --> 00:13:16,860
And hydrophobic parts tuck
themselves inside away from it.

360
00:13:16,860 --> 00:13:19,830
They then form these tiny
structures called micelles.

361
00:13:19,830 --> 00:13:23,130
And the micelles cluster
together into larger globules.

362
00:13:23,130 --> 00:13:25,383
These globules next
enter the spinning duct.

363
00:13:26,520 --> 00:13:30,600
- For the dragline silk, the
duct is kind of S-shaped,

364
00:13:30,600 --> 00:13:33,180
but it gets skinnier and skinnier.

365
00:13:33,180 --> 00:13:35,010
- [Henry] As the globules
go through the narrow duct,

366
00:13:35,010 --> 00:13:37,620
the liquid near the walls
rubs against the surface,

367
00:13:37,620 --> 00:13:38,820
and it moves more slowly,

368
00:13:38,820 --> 00:13:41,190
while the liquid in the
middle moves faster.

369
00:13:41,190 --> 00:13:42,930
So the layers slide past each other,

370
00:13:42,930 --> 00:13:44,460
which is known as shear.

371
00:13:44,460 --> 00:13:47,730
These shear forces stretch
and deform the globule.

372
00:13:47,730 --> 00:13:51,630
- You also remove some
water, so water goes out.

373
00:13:51,630 --> 00:13:56,630
You get a drop in pH, so it
becomes a little bit more acidic

374
00:13:56,981 --> 00:13:59,060
as you go down this duct.

375
00:13:59,060 --> 00:14:00,720
- So the proteins are then being changed

376
00:14:00,720 --> 00:14:01,800
in two ways at once.

377
00:14:01,800 --> 00:14:04,050
Mechanically, they're
being pulled and aligned.

378
00:14:04,050 --> 00:14:05,700
And chemically, that drop in pH

379
00:14:05,700 --> 00:14:08,160
means that there are now
more positive hydronium ions

380
00:14:08,160 --> 00:14:09,660
in the solution.

381
00:14:09,660 --> 00:14:11,790
These bind to the negative
parts of the proteins,

382
00:14:11,790 --> 00:14:13,170
neutralizing them.

383
00:14:13,170 --> 00:14:15,900
Now all the proteins don't
repel each other as strongly,

384
00:14:15,900 --> 00:14:18,090
and so the N-terminal ends begin pairing,

385
00:14:18,090 --> 00:14:20,490
linking the proteins into long chains.

386
00:14:20,490 --> 00:14:22,410
These chains are pulled
through a tiny narrowing

387
00:14:22,410 --> 00:14:25,200
called the drawdown taper,
which leads to the spigot.

388
00:14:25,200 --> 00:14:27,900
Here, the spider pulls the
liquid through a small opening.

389
00:14:27,900 --> 00:14:29,730
This forces the liquid to speed up.

390
00:14:29,730 --> 00:14:31,800
And as it speeds up, it stretches.

391
00:14:31,800 --> 00:14:34,290
It's this final stretch that
pulls neighboring spidroins

392
00:14:34,290 --> 00:14:36,120
tightly alongside one another.

393
00:14:36,120 --> 00:14:38,250
Now, depending on the
sequence of amino acids,

394
00:14:38,250 --> 00:14:41,010
some sections fold into zigzag strands.

395
00:14:41,010 --> 00:14:42,360
These strands then interlock

396
00:14:42,360 --> 00:14:44,910
and rows of hydrogen bonds
stitch them into rigid,

397
00:14:44,910 --> 00:14:46,230
sheet-like structures,

398
00:14:46,230 --> 00:14:48,210
which stack together into the nanocrystals

399
00:14:48,210 --> 00:14:50,400
that give the spider silk its strength.

400
00:14:50,400 --> 00:14:53,310
In other sections, the
spidroins don't fold as neatly.

401
00:14:53,310 --> 00:14:54,870
That's how you get the amorphous regions

402
00:14:54,870 --> 00:14:56,880
which give the silk its stretch.

403
00:14:56,880 --> 00:14:58,500
Exactly how the proteins assemble

404
00:14:58,500 --> 00:15:00,630
inside the spinning duct
is still being studied.

405
00:15:00,630 --> 00:15:02,340
No one fully understands it yet,

406
00:15:02,340 --> 00:15:03,960
and that makes recreating the process

407
00:15:03,960 --> 00:15:05,280
in a lab quite difficult.

408
00:15:05,280 --> 00:15:06,337
So scientists wondered,

409
00:15:06,337 --> 00:15:08,310
"What if instead of starting from scratch,

410
00:15:08,310 --> 00:15:11,340
you used an animal that
already has a spinner?"

411
00:15:11,340 --> 00:15:12,870
This is exactly what researchers

412
00:15:12,870 --> 00:15:14,460
at Kraig BioCraft Laboratories,

413
00:15:14,460 --> 00:15:17,190
a biotech company in Michigan,
have been working on.

414
00:15:17,190 --> 00:15:18,930
What's more, they're
doing it with an insect

415
00:15:18,930 --> 00:15:21,873
that humans have been farming
for nearly 5,000 years.

416
00:15:23,220 --> 00:15:24,240
According to legend,

417
00:15:24,240 --> 00:15:26,760
a Chinese empress was
relaxing in her garden,

418
00:15:26,760 --> 00:15:28,920
when something fell into her teacup.

419
00:15:28,920 --> 00:15:31,500
She looked inside, and saw a cocoon.

420
00:15:31,500 --> 00:15:32,760
The hot water loosened it.

421
00:15:32,760 --> 00:15:34,020
And when she lifted it out,

422
00:15:34,020 --> 00:15:36,810
it unraveled into a
single shimmering thread.

423
00:15:36,810 --> 00:15:39,870
So long that it stretched
across her entire garden.

424
00:15:39,870 --> 00:15:41,580
This was silk.

425
00:15:41,580 --> 00:15:42,870
Whether or not that story's true,

426
00:15:42,870 --> 00:15:44,910
people eventually learned
to farm the insect

427
00:15:44,910 --> 00:15:46,202
that made the thread.

428
00:15:46,202 --> 00:15:47,880
(jaunty music)
Silkworms.

429
00:15:47,880 --> 00:15:50,580
They're the caterpillars of
the domesticated silk moth.

430
00:15:50,580 --> 00:15:53,010
Silk quickly became one of
the most valuable materials

431
00:15:53,010 --> 00:15:53,843
in the land.

432
00:15:53,843 --> 00:15:55,590
It dressed emperors and spurred trade

433
00:15:55,590 --> 00:15:57,300
connecting East Asia and Europe.

434
00:15:57,300 --> 00:15:59,700
So much so that it gave
the trade route its name,

435
00:15:59,700 --> 00:16:01,380
the Silk Road.

436
00:16:01,380 --> 00:16:04,395
For nearly 2,000 years,
China guarded the secret.

437
00:16:04,395 --> 00:16:07,233
But of course, people were
always trying to steal it.

438
00:16:08,730 --> 00:16:09,900
By the mid-sixth century,

439
00:16:09,900 --> 00:16:12,060
the Byzantine Empire was in trouble.

440
00:16:12,060 --> 00:16:13,860
Plague had devastated the population.

441
00:16:13,860 --> 00:16:14,700
And on top of that,

442
00:16:14,700 --> 00:16:17,370
the purchase of silk
was draining its gold.

443
00:16:17,370 --> 00:16:19,860
The problem was that
Byzantines couldn't make silk.

444
00:16:19,860 --> 00:16:21,510
Most of it had to come through Persia,

445
00:16:21,510 --> 00:16:23,820
the very empire it was fighting.

446
00:16:23,820 --> 00:16:27,180
So Emperor Justinian made a
secret deal with two monks.

447
00:16:27,180 --> 00:16:29,430
They would travel east,
find the source of silk,

448
00:16:29,430 --> 00:16:31,290
and then smuggle it back.

449
00:16:31,290 --> 00:16:32,640
They returned with a secret

450
00:16:32,640 --> 00:16:34,920
hidden inside their hollow canes.

451
00:16:34,920 --> 00:16:36,420
Silkworm eggs.

452
00:16:36,420 --> 00:16:37,950
This may be the first recorded case

453
00:16:37,950 --> 00:16:39,990
of industrial espionage in history.

454
00:16:39,990 --> 00:16:42,693
With that, Byzantium could
finally make its own silk.

455
00:16:43,650 --> 00:16:45,810
Nowadays, we farm them by the millions.

456
00:16:45,810 --> 00:16:48,030
- One moth lays 500 eggs.
- [Henry] Okay.

457
00:16:48,030 --> 00:16:50,520
- So when you talk about
growing productions, right?

458
00:16:50,520 --> 00:16:53,250
Like my wife and I had a baby.

459
00:16:53,250 --> 00:16:55,500
These guys, they have 500 babies.

460
00:16:55,500 --> 00:16:57,090
And they do it every 30 days.

461
00:16:57,090 --> 00:16:58,897
- So the researchers at Kraig wondered,

462
00:16:58,897 --> 00:17:00,390
"What if we could make the silkworm

463
00:17:00,390 --> 00:17:02,340
spin spider silk instead?"

464
00:17:02,340 --> 00:17:04,530
- When we create a transgenic silkworm,

465
00:17:04,530 --> 00:17:06,720
we're taking the genetics of a silkworm,

466
00:17:06,720 --> 00:17:07,950
and the genetics of a spider,

467
00:17:07,950 --> 00:17:08,940
and we're putting those together.

468
00:17:08,940 --> 00:17:10,710
We're taking the best aspects of both.

469
00:17:10,710 --> 00:17:12,660
And that's what we're
doing to create our fibers.

470
00:17:12,660 --> 00:17:14,640
- [Henry] They start by
gluing eggs onto a slide,

471
00:17:14,640 --> 00:17:16,500
which they line up under a microscope.

472
00:17:16,500 --> 00:17:18,150
- So this is the microinjection station.

473
00:17:18,150 --> 00:17:19,140
We're talking about eggs

474
00:17:19,140 --> 00:17:21,000
that are the size of the head of a pen.

475
00:17:21,000 --> 00:17:22,080
We're talking about needles

476
00:17:22,080 --> 00:17:23,820
that are half a micron in diameter.

477
00:17:23,820 --> 00:17:26,940
- This part is the, I want to inject.

478
00:17:26,940 --> 00:17:29,310
So as you see, this is the tungsten needle

479
00:17:29,310 --> 00:17:32,370
and this is the glass capillary.

480
00:17:32,370 --> 00:17:36,300
And first we poke a hole
with the tungsten needle.

481
00:17:36,300 --> 00:17:41,300
I will actually move the eggs
to the capillary and poke.

482
00:17:41,640 --> 00:17:43,410
- The fluid carrying the spider DNA

483
00:17:43,410 --> 00:17:45,150
is then injected into the part of the egg

484
00:17:45,150 --> 00:17:47,520
that will eventually become the silkworm.

485
00:17:47,520 --> 00:17:49,560
But at this point, the
genes are still separate.

486
00:17:49,560 --> 00:17:52,020
They have to become part
of the silkworm's own DNA.

487
00:17:52,020 --> 00:17:54,570
And luckily, nature already
has a way of doing that.

488
00:17:54,570 --> 00:17:56,130
If you take an insect like a moth

489
00:17:56,130 --> 00:17:57,430
and look inside its genome,

490
00:17:57,430 --> 00:18:00,840
you'll see some stretches
of DNA that move around.

491
00:18:00,840 --> 00:18:03,540
They jump from one place
in the genome to another.

492
00:18:03,540 --> 00:18:06,780
These are called jumping
genes, or transposons.

493
00:18:06,780 --> 00:18:08,910
One specific one is called piggyBac,

494
00:18:08,910 --> 00:18:12,240
and it was first identified
in a cabbage looper moth.

495
00:18:12,240 --> 00:18:13,680
PiggyBac is a piece of DNA

496
00:18:13,680 --> 00:18:15,570
with two short sequences at its ends,

497
00:18:15,570 --> 00:18:17,010
and it works together with an enzyme

498
00:18:17,010 --> 00:18:19,950
that recognizes these ends,
cuts the whole piece out,

499
00:18:19,950 --> 00:18:22,200
and inserts it somewhere
else in the genome,

500
00:18:22,200 --> 00:18:24,570
kind of like a natural
cut and paste system.

501
00:18:24,570 --> 00:18:26,460
What scientists realized
is that if the enzyme

502
00:18:26,460 --> 00:18:28,080
only looks at the two ends,

503
00:18:28,080 --> 00:18:29,760
then you can keep those ends the same,

504
00:18:29,760 --> 00:18:31,620
but change what sits in the middle,

505
00:18:31,620 --> 00:18:34,200
and use that to implant
the DNA of your choosing.

506
00:18:34,200 --> 00:18:36,180
So in the lab, the DNA in the middle

507
00:18:36,180 --> 00:18:38,310
is replaced with the spider silk gene.

508
00:18:38,310 --> 00:18:39,990
This, together with separate instructions

509
00:18:39,990 --> 00:18:40,950
for making the enzyme,

510
00:18:40,950 --> 00:18:43,590
is what's then injected
into the silkworm egg.

511
00:18:43,590 --> 00:18:44,520
And inside the egg,

512
00:18:44,520 --> 00:18:47,340
the enzyme recognizes the
familiar end sequences and cuts

513
00:18:47,340 --> 00:18:50,940
and inserts the spider silk
gene into the silkworm's DNA.

514
00:18:50,940 --> 00:18:52,920
If everything works, it
becomes a permanent part

515
00:18:52,920 --> 00:18:54,170
of the silkworm's genome.

516
00:18:55,260 --> 00:18:56,850
Now with silkworm where the edit worked

517
00:18:56,850 --> 00:18:59,280
looks almost exactly
like one where it didn't.

518
00:18:59,280 --> 00:19:00,420
- [Jon] The first approach we used

519
00:19:00,420 --> 00:19:03,690
was creating transgenics
with the glowing cocoon.

520
00:19:03,690 --> 00:19:07,140
A green fluorescent protein is
what's making these guys glow

521
00:19:07,140 --> 00:19:09,309
that green color under
this particular wavelength

522
00:19:09,309 --> 00:19:11,970
with that particular light
filter in front of it.

523
00:19:11,970 --> 00:19:13,980
- [Henry] It feels magical.

524
00:19:13,980 --> 00:19:15,360
And there's a living thing inside of it.

525
00:19:15,360 --> 00:19:16,193
- [Jon] Mm hmm, yep.

526
00:19:16,193 --> 00:19:17,880
- [Henry] And it's creating
the glowing effect.

527
00:19:17,880 --> 00:19:18,713
- [Jon] Yeah.

528
00:19:18,713 --> 00:19:21,180
- [Henry] But even if the
DNA insertion is successful,

529
00:19:21,180 --> 00:19:23,640
it might not have ended
up in the right place.

530
00:19:23,640 --> 00:19:25,440
- If I create the world's best recipe

531
00:19:25,440 --> 00:19:26,790
for chocolate chip cookies,

532
00:19:26,790 --> 00:19:28,440
and I stick it in the pasta section-

533
00:19:28,440 --> 00:19:29,273
- [Henry] Yeah.

534
00:19:29,273 --> 00:19:30,106
- You're probably not going to make

535
00:19:30,106 --> 00:19:30,939
a lot of chocolate chip cookies, right?

536
00:19:30,939 --> 00:19:31,860
'Cause you're not going to see it.

537
00:19:31,860 --> 00:19:33,570
- [Henry] Yeah.
- Same thing for this, right?

538
00:19:33,570 --> 00:19:35,700
We want the recipe in the right section

539
00:19:35,700 --> 00:19:36,900
of the right cookbook.

540
00:19:36,900 --> 00:19:38,550
- That's why getting the spider silk gene

541
00:19:38,550 --> 00:19:40,661
into the silkworm isn't enough.

542
00:19:40,661 --> 00:19:43,470
- We really want the spider
silk get incorporated

543
00:19:43,470 --> 00:19:47,640
into their silk gland,
not any other tissue.

544
00:19:47,640 --> 00:19:49,440
- [Henry] But piggyBac only looks

545
00:19:49,440 --> 00:19:51,330
for a four-letter DNA sequence.

546
00:19:51,330 --> 00:19:52,860
TTAA.

547
00:19:52,860 --> 00:19:56,640
- There's so many TTAA in their genome.

548
00:19:56,640 --> 00:19:59,190
You couldn't really
control where they were.

549
00:19:59,190 --> 00:20:00,720
- [Henry] So it's like there
are a lot of different places

550
00:20:00,720 --> 00:20:03,720
where they could park.
- Yeah, yeah, that's true!

551
00:20:03,720 --> 00:20:06,360
- And that means that it
won't spin pure spider silk.

552
00:20:06,360 --> 00:20:08,910
If you had to estimate,
of the transgenic silk,

553
00:20:08,910 --> 00:20:10,500
like what percentage is spider DNA?

554
00:20:10,500 --> 00:20:13,350
- Like 6%, 10%.
- That's insane to me!

555
00:20:13,350 --> 00:20:15,240
So even with this limited gene transfer,

556
00:20:15,240 --> 00:20:17,850
the fibers still achieve much
of the mechanical performance

557
00:20:17,850 --> 00:20:19,050
of pure spider silk.

558
00:20:19,050 --> 00:20:21,750
- Our average samples are usually about

559
00:20:21,750 --> 00:20:24,060
60% of spider silk, right?

560
00:20:24,060 --> 00:20:26,730
Which, show me any
other place in the world

561
00:20:26,730 --> 00:20:29,280
where you can get materials
that perform at 60% the strength

562
00:20:29,280 --> 00:20:31,620
of spider silk that you can
make cost effectively, right?

563
00:20:31,620 --> 00:20:33,660
- [Henry] To push the
60% average even higher,

564
00:20:33,660 --> 00:20:35,790
the insertion needs to be more targeted.

565
00:20:35,790 --> 00:20:38,010
- The next step is to create pure,

566
00:20:38,010 --> 00:20:39,690
what are called
knock-in/knockout transgenics

567
00:20:39,690 --> 00:20:42,270
where we will completely
remove all aspects

568
00:20:42,270 --> 00:20:44,340
of the silkworm's native DNA for the silk,

569
00:20:44,340 --> 00:20:46,830
and replace that completely
with the spider silk protein.

570
00:20:46,830 --> 00:20:49,050
- And to do that, most of
the leading labs in the field

571
00:20:49,050 --> 00:20:51,344
are exploring CRISPR-Cas9.

572
00:20:51,344 --> 00:20:53,310
This tool has two parts.

573
00:20:53,310 --> 00:20:55,800
The first is a guide, a
short piece of genetic code

574
00:20:55,800 --> 00:20:58,380
designed to match one
exact stretch of DNA.

575
00:20:58,380 --> 00:20:59,280
Unlike piggyBac,

576
00:20:59,280 --> 00:21:02,370
which recognizes a sequence
just four DNA letters long,

577
00:21:02,370 --> 00:21:04,200
this guide matches about 20 letters,

578
00:21:04,200 --> 00:21:06,270
making it far more specific.

579
00:21:06,270 --> 00:21:07,950
The second is a cutting protein.

580
00:21:07,950 --> 00:21:09,660
When the guide finds
its matching sequence,

581
00:21:09,660 --> 00:21:11,490
the protein cuts the DNA.

582
00:21:11,490 --> 00:21:13,860
Here, that spot is inside
the silkworm's own gene

583
00:21:13,860 --> 00:21:15,120
for making silk.

584
00:21:15,120 --> 00:21:17,280
The cell immediately
tries to repair the break,

585
00:21:17,280 --> 00:21:18,750
and scientists take advantage of this

586
00:21:18,750 --> 00:21:22,770
by also injecting donor DNA,
carrying the spider silk gene.

587
00:21:22,770 --> 00:21:26,100
As the cell repairs the cut,
it copies in that donor DNA,

588
00:21:26,100 --> 00:21:27,480
stitching the spider silk gene

589
00:21:27,480 --> 00:21:29,790
into this one precise location.

590
00:21:29,790 --> 00:21:31,920
But this process is still
an active development.

591
00:21:31,920 --> 00:21:33,300
And Kraig is not the only group

592
00:21:33,300 --> 00:21:35,340
chasing the dream of spider silk.

593
00:21:35,340 --> 00:21:38,160
In Germany, AMSilk is
making proteins for fibers,

594
00:21:38,160 --> 00:21:40,470
coatings, powders, and hydrogels.

595
00:21:40,470 --> 00:21:42,900
And in Japan, Spiber is
brewing protein fibers

596
00:21:42,900 --> 00:21:44,250
through fermentation.

597
00:21:44,250 --> 00:21:46,170
Brands like Goldwin and The North Face

598
00:21:46,170 --> 00:21:48,030
have already used a
version of these fibers

599
00:21:48,030 --> 00:21:49,050
in their clothing.

600
00:21:49,050 --> 00:21:51,060
And the military has been interested too.

601
00:21:51,060 --> 00:21:53,250
In 2016, the US Army funded Kraig

602
00:21:53,250 --> 00:21:54,870
to produce ballistic shoe packs,

603
00:21:54,870 --> 00:21:56,850
panels layered with transgenic silk

604
00:21:56,850 --> 00:21:59,310
that are designed as potential body armor.

605
00:21:59,310 --> 00:22:01,740
And it's even being explored in medicine.

606
00:22:01,740 --> 00:22:02,573
For centuries,

607
00:22:02,573 --> 00:22:04,980
surgeons have stitched
wounds together with silk.

608
00:22:04,980 --> 00:22:07,920
But now a company called
Newrotex is using spider silk

609
00:22:07,920 --> 00:22:10,230
to help repair damaged nerves.

610
00:22:10,230 --> 00:22:11,730
So if it can be produced cheaply,

611
00:22:11,730 --> 00:22:13,710
spider silk could find
its way into clothing,

612
00:22:13,710 --> 00:22:16,950
armor, implants, even nerve repair.

613
00:22:16,950 --> 00:22:19,020
But to do that, we're
going to need a lot of it.

614
00:22:19,020 --> 00:22:24,020
- And this is our specialized
spider silk. There you go.

615
00:22:24,660 --> 00:22:25,553
- This is the transgenic spider silk.

616
00:22:25,553 --> 00:22:26,880
- [Jon] This is spider silk.

617
00:22:26,880 --> 00:22:28,036
This is transgenic spider silk.

618
00:22:28,036 --> 00:22:29,100
- What? This is like a bale.

619
00:22:29,100 --> 00:22:30,660
This is a hay bale of spider silk.

620
00:22:30,660 --> 00:22:35,070
- So last year we produced
about a half a ton

621
00:22:35,070 --> 00:22:37,080
of spider silk cocoon.
- Half a ton.

622
00:22:37,080 --> 00:22:38,790
- And this is silk from that.

623
00:22:38,790 --> 00:22:40,290
- But what about our original question?

624
00:22:40,290 --> 00:22:44,400
Can you use transgenic spider
silk to swing like Spider-Man?

625
00:22:44,400 --> 00:22:47,430
So Derek, I've got you
here in a climbing gym

626
00:22:47,430 --> 00:22:49,350
for a very good reason.

627
00:22:49,350 --> 00:22:52,080
And the reason is underneath
this dirty dish towel.

628
00:22:52,080 --> 00:22:53,880
- Unveil it, unveil it. Yeah, go.

629
00:22:53,880 --> 00:22:58,650
All right, okay. This
looks very uninspiring.

630
00:22:58,650 --> 00:23:00,090
- [Henry] So what's interesting is

631
00:23:00,090 --> 00:23:02,250
this is one continuous filament.

632
00:23:02,250 --> 00:23:03,780
- This is just one strand.

633
00:23:03,780 --> 00:23:05,070
- But each one of these strands

634
00:23:05,070 --> 00:23:07,770
is actually 10 individual silk filaments

635
00:23:07,770 --> 00:23:09,660
that are kind of connected.
- All right.

636
00:23:09,660 --> 00:23:11,520
So you want me to hang from this?

637
00:23:11,520 --> 00:23:13,260
- I do want you to hang from it, yes.

638
00:23:13,260 --> 00:23:14,730
I actually want you to do
more than just hang from it.

639
00:23:14,730 --> 00:23:16,440
I want you to swing.

640
00:23:16,440 --> 00:23:18,270
- This will be the first time ever

641
00:23:18,270 --> 00:23:22,140
anyone has ever swung
from actual spider silk.

642
00:23:22,140 --> 00:23:25,174
Granted this spider silk came
from other organisms, but...

643
00:23:25,174 --> 00:23:28,091
(mysterious music)

644
00:23:29,644 --> 00:23:32,310
I don't know if it's going to
hold my weight, so let's see.

645
00:23:32,310 --> 00:23:34,863
In three, two, one.

646
00:23:40,650 --> 00:23:43,900
- You really came close!
(Derek and Henry laughing)

647
00:23:43,900 --> 00:23:46,650
(dramatic music)

648
00:23:53,819 --> 00:23:57,402
(dramatic music continues)

649
00:23:58,980 --> 00:24:02,337
- Don't tell anyone, but Spider-Man.

650
00:24:02,337 --> 00:24:05,087
(dramatic music)

651
00:24:07,260 --> 00:24:09,510
- Okay, so we've seen
it can hold your weight

652
00:24:09,510 --> 00:24:10,410
pretty reasonably.

653
00:24:10,410 --> 00:24:13,140
We could swing, but I do want
to put it to the ultimate test

654
00:24:13,140 --> 00:24:15,000
and get you up there.

655
00:24:15,000 --> 00:24:16,350
How much do you trust spider silk?

656
00:24:16,350 --> 00:24:18,060
- Tensile strength doesn't lie.

657
00:24:18,060 --> 00:24:20,371
- All right, let's get you up there.

658
00:24:20,371 --> 00:24:21,750
(tense music)

659
00:24:21,750 --> 00:24:22,987
- We used the title,

660
00:24:22,987 --> 00:24:26,378
"Risking my life to settle
a physics debate" too early.

661
00:24:26,378 --> 00:24:28,878
(tense music)

662
00:24:31,020 --> 00:24:33,420
It feels like it's going
to dig into my fingers.

663
00:24:34,560 --> 00:24:37,563
- [Speaker] This is crazy.
(tense music)

664
00:24:46,678 --> 00:24:47,970
(tense music continues)
(Derek yelling)

665
00:24:47,970 --> 00:24:50,478
- I'm going to go. I'm going to go!

666
00:24:50,478 --> 00:24:52,260
(tense music)

667
00:24:52,260 --> 00:24:54,270
- [Henry] Whoo!
(Derek yelling)

668
00:24:54,270 --> 00:24:55,103
Let's go!

669
00:24:57,443 --> 00:24:59,223
- You got to see my finger, man!

670
00:25:00,240 --> 00:25:01,140
- [Henry] Ooh, damn!

671
00:25:01,140 --> 00:25:05,310
- Yeah. This is the
problem with spider silk.

672
00:25:05,310 --> 00:25:09,120
Just, it's thin, it's strong,

673
00:25:09,120 --> 00:25:11,400
and it just rips you open.

674
00:25:11,400 --> 00:25:12,450
- Now, if it isn't clear,

675
00:25:12,450 --> 00:25:14,970
we're not exactly web-swinging experts.

676
00:25:14,970 --> 00:25:16,830
But we'd love to get the
silk into of the hands

677
00:25:16,830 --> 00:25:18,060
of someone who is.

678
00:25:18,060 --> 00:25:19,980
- Tom Holland, this is a challenge.

679
00:25:19,980 --> 00:25:21,270
Yeah, I'm calling out Tom Holland.

680
00:25:21,270 --> 00:25:22,620
I'm calling out all them guys.

681
00:25:22,620 --> 00:25:25,353
Andrew Garfield, Tobey McGuire.

682
00:25:27,000 --> 00:25:29,253
That's right. Come at me, bro.

683
00:25:30,579 --> 00:25:33,794
(electronic music)

684
00:25:33,794 --> 00:25:35,040
- See, spider silk is so strong

685
00:25:35,040 --> 00:25:37,380
and so thin that it
actually cut Derek's skin.

686
00:25:37,380 --> 00:25:38,520
And that's actually a great way

687
00:25:38,520 --> 00:25:40,920
to explain the design
flaw with modern razors.

688
00:25:40,920 --> 00:25:43,260
Thanks to Henson Shaving
for sponsoring this video.

689
00:25:43,260 --> 00:25:45,300
See, facial hair resists
more than you think.

690
00:25:45,300 --> 00:25:47,940
And many razor blades
are engineered so thin

691
00:25:47,940 --> 00:25:49,800
that they bend under that resistance.

692
00:25:49,800 --> 00:25:51,390
This is called blade flex.

693
00:25:51,390 --> 00:25:53,700
Now, most razors actually
build this flex in.

694
00:25:53,700 --> 00:25:55,350
They use springs, pivots,

695
00:25:55,350 --> 00:25:58,110
and flexible mounts that
allow the blade to move.

696
00:25:58,110 --> 00:26:00,300
It's supposed to make
the shave feel gentler,

697
00:26:00,300 --> 00:26:02,790
but it means that the cutting
angle is constantly changing.

698
00:26:02,790 --> 00:26:05,070
When unsupported, the
blade bends mid-stroke

699
00:26:05,070 --> 00:26:06,930
and instead of slicing cleanly,

700
00:26:06,930 --> 00:26:09,450
it tugs the hairs, micro-cutting the skin.

701
00:26:09,450 --> 00:26:11,340
That's what causes irritation.

702
00:26:11,340 --> 00:26:14,820
The usual fixes are lubrication
strips or extra blades,

703
00:26:14,820 --> 00:26:16,560
but they don't solve the real problem.

704
00:26:16,560 --> 00:26:18,570
The blade is still allowed to flex.

705
00:26:18,570 --> 00:26:21,150
We assume that razor bumps
and irritation are inevitable,

706
00:26:21,150 --> 00:26:23,043
but that's shaped by bad design.

707
00:26:23,910 --> 00:26:26,310
But Henson is designed
by aerospace machinists

708
00:26:26,310 --> 00:26:28,740
who control cutting forces
with high precision.

709
00:26:28,740 --> 00:26:31,950
And their razors use a single
precisely-machined blade.

710
00:26:31,950 --> 00:26:32,880
Instead of letting it move,

711
00:26:32,880 --> 00:26:34,800
Henson's design supports the cutting edge

712
00:26:34,800 --> 00:26:36,480
with tight machining tolerances,

713
00:26:36,480 --> 00:26:39,090
holding the blade securely
so the angle is consistent.

714
00:26:39,090 --> 00:26:41,370
Remove the flex, remove the irritation.

715
00:26:41,370 --> 00:26:43,410
Use code "Veritasium" for 100 free blades

716
00:26:43,410 --> 00:26:44,520
with any razor purchase.

717
00:26:44,520 --> 00:26:46,590
Just add both the razor
and blades to your cart.

718
00:26:46,590 --> 00:26:47,580
Thanks to Henson Shaving,

719
00:26:47,580 --> 00:26:49,353
and as always, thanks for watching.
